{{Quote|An attractive cagebird, the NEIMOIDIAN PYLAT BIRD has a melodious soothing song. It is very territorial. Native to the Neimoidian mountains.|Lyrre T'enna|<ref name="WFG" />}}
The '''pylat bird''', also referred to as '''pylat''', was a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Bird/Legends|avian]] from [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidia]]. Because of their white plumage and harmonious song, pylats were prized cagebirds among the richer members of the [[galactic community]]. The status-obsessed [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]] in particular considered the possession of pylats as an outward sign of power and wealth. A rare breed with red-spotted plumage also dwelled on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Sojourn (moon)|Sojourn]]. The latter breed was looked at with even more envy, and the gift of one such pylat played an instrumental role in forging the alliance between [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] and the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Clawed_pylat.png|thumb|left|180px|A clawed pylat bird.]]
Pylats were medium-sized, [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Bird/Legends|avians]] native to the [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]] of [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidia]]. They had four [[Limb/Legends|limbs]]: two legs and two wings that doubled as arms, the first joint of which was tipped with a four-fingered clawed "hand." The top of their head was crowned by a showy and prominent feather crest. Most commonly, pylats had a predominantly [[Color/Legends|white]] plumage with colored features in the crest, cheeks and neck. They also had a long and broad tail that could be white<ref name="WFG" /> or display darker colors.<ref name="E1VG">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> A rarer breed dwelling in the forests of [[Sojourn (moon)|Sojourn]] sported a red-spotted white plumage.<ref name="DP" />Being birds, the pylats produced [[Egg/Legends|eggs]] that developped and hatched outside the maternal body,<ref name="DOP Decoded">{{TCW|Defenders of Peace|d=y}}</ref> and were [[Endothermy|endothermic]] creatures,<ref name="Endo" /> burning [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] within themselves to control their body temperature.<ref name="SWSA">''[[Star Wars Science Adventures: Journey Across Planet X]]''</ref>

==Behavior==
[[File:Symyrthi.jpg|thumb|A Sy Myrthian with a pylat on the hand]]
{{Quote|And yet he appears to be at home in his new environment.''"<br />"''His songs suggest as much.|Sidious and Gunray|<ref name="DP" />}}
In their natural environment, the pylats used their prominent headcrests for display purposes.<ref name="E1VG" /> While they were very defensive of their territory, they were considered attractive by bird enthusiasts, and could be domesticated.<ref name="WFG" /> Their song was very harmonious and soothing to the [[Ear/Legends|ears]]&mdash;so much that one could use the quality of a pylat's song to assess its general level of contentment.<ref name="DP" />Pet pylats could be confined in [[Neimoidian bird cage|special cages]] fitted with [[Force field/Legends|stasis field]] generators,<ref name="E1VG" /> although some owners would take their bird for a walk while carrying on the hand.<ref name="WFG" />

==History==
{{Quote|You value the bird—this symbol of wealth.''"<br />"''I am the envy of my peers for possessing it.|Sidious and Gunray|<ref name="DP" />}}
The common pylat birds evolved on Neimoidia, a planet located in the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The sentient inhabitants of that world, a [[Near-Duros]] species called the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]], came to associate the pylats with wealth and status, creating covetousness amongst those who did not possess such birds.<ref name="DP" /> Their fatty eggs were also a delicacy in Neimoidian cuisine.<ref name="DOP Decoded" /> At some point in history, the pylat also found their way to Sojourn,<ref name="DP" />a moon located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> where they evolved into a distinct breed.<ref name="DP" />

==Pylats in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Gunray is fond of pylats, which the Neimoidians associate with wealth.|Darth Plagueis, to his apprentice|<ref name="DP" />}}
[[File:HaakoGunrayPalpy-Ep1.png|thumb|left|The gift of a pylat bird helped forge the alliance between Darth Sidious and the Trade Federation.]]
Because of their white plumage and soothing song, the pylat birds were prized as pets by the wealthier beings of the galaxy.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|51|pylat bird}}</ref> During the last decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], a red-spotted pylat became part of a plot that ultimately sealed the galaxy's fate. Wishing to ally themselves with the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] in order to bring their [[Grand Plan/Legends|Grand Plan]] to fruition, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] had a pylat bird from Sojourn delivered to [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] of the Trade Federation. At first, the rare bird confused Gunray, who could not track its origin, but he was pleased with the gift and it soon occupied pride of place in his office, and Gunray savored the envy of his colleagues had for the bird.<ref name="DP" />

Shortly afterwards, Plagueis' [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]&mdash;whose public face was that of [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] Palpatine of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]&mdash;then contacted Gunray by [[Holovid/Legends|holo]] and claimed responsibility for sending the bird, which then opened a broader discussion. Because Gunray was unfamiliar with the [[Force power/Legends|powers]] of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]], Sidious threatened to demonstrate them by [[Death/Legends|killing]] the pylat from a remote location. Gunray soon saw the advantage of complying with Sidious' will. However, Sidious and Plagueis had actually fooled Gunray completely. It was not actually a bird from Sojourn, but rather a [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of a red-spotted pylat from Sojourn created on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]&mdash;one of the many tests Plagueis had the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]] perform in preparation for the eventual order of an [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|army of clones]].<ref name="DP" />

Later, when the Federation [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|blockaded]] Naboo under Sidious' orders, Gunray had several caged pylats in the conference room of his [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']]. When he flooded the room with [[Dioxis/Legends|poisonous gas]] in a failed attempt to murder [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], the birds dropped dead in their cage, giving the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] a visual cue of the danger.<ref name="TPMN">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref>

Despite their long-established popularity amongst the socialites, pylat birds were never displayed at the [[Coruscant Livestock Exchange and Exhibition]] until after the establishment of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]<ref name="WFG" /> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Following exhibition there, a [[Sy Myrthian/Legends|Sy Myrthian]] [[Unidentified New Republic Sy Myrthian diplomat|diplomat]] had a pet pylat bird. The illustrious [[Zoologist/Legends|zoologist]] [[Lyrre T'enna]] made on-the-fly renderings of pylats that were included in the published edition of [[Lyrre T'enna's annotated field guide|her field guide]].<ref name="WFG" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Hyperspace_cagebird.jpg|thumb|Terryl Whitlatch's concept art of a "Neimoidian Cage Bird"]]
Several exotic cagebirds were first slated to appear in the [[1999]] movie [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. They were to appear at the beginning of the movie, during the scene where the Jedi ambassadors notice the presence of poisonous gas in the conference room. The pylats were supposed to drop dead in their cages, alerting the Jedi of the gas attack. However,
the movie staff ended up judging that the presence of birds in a negotiation room during a blockade did not look appropriate, and neither was the idea that Jedi needed this to detect gas.<ref name="NCB">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/galactic/2006/01/galactic20060120.html|series=Galactic Gallery|text=Neimoidian Cage Bird}}</ref> While that footage was left on the cutting room's floor,<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> it was still present in [[Terry Brooks]]' [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]] of ''The Phantom Menace'', which was released shortly before the movie itself.<ref name="TPMN" /> Original production artwork by [[Terryl Whitlatch]] dated February [[1997]] depicted the Neimoidian birds as [[Wikipedia:Phoenix (mythology)|phoenix]]-like creatures displaying flowing red feathers with eye-shaped purple spots.<ref name="NCB" />

The exotic birds cut from ''The Phantom Menace'' were first shown in their current appearance and identified as "pylat birds" in [[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary|''Star Wars: Episode I The Visual Dictionary'']], written by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]]. According to the fan website [http://www.starwarz.com/tbone T-Bone's Star Wars Universe], Reynolds derived that term from the name of Laura Pylat, one of his good friends from the [[Wikipedia:University of Michigan|University of Michigan]].<ref name="Laura Pylat">{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarz.com/tbone/archive/index.php?categoryid=12&p2_articleid=207|text=Pylat Birds|author=T-Bone|date=2005-03-16|work=T-Bone's Star Wars Universe|nobackup=1}}</ref>

In the 2000s, Neimoidian bird cages could be purchased in the ''[[Star Wars]]''-themed [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|MMORPG]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'',
but those were empty. Once again, the pylat did not make the final cut.<ref name="gal">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> They ''did'', however, make the final cut of the [[2012]] novel [[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']], where they were mentioned by name, and were key to the first face-to-face holovid between Nute Gunray and Darth Sidious.<ref name="DP" />
